paper_diagnosis: Disseminated cryptococcosis revealing an HIV infection
disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated cryptococcosis with neuro-meningeal and pulmonary involvement revealing HIV infection
presentation_summary: 31-year-old woman with three months of progressively worsening holocranial headache, fever, asthenia, anorexia, and weight loss.
Two weeks later she developed sudden persistent hearing loss, vomiting, cough, and dyspnea.
Exam showed fever, preserved consciousness, hemodynamic stability, nuchal rigidity, Brudzinski sign, hypoxia requiring oxygen, and crackles.
Chest CT showed right apical excavated lesion, pulmonary nodules/micronodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
CSF, sputum, and blood culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans; serum and CSF cryptococcal antigen were positive; HIV was newly confirmed.
She received amphotericin B plus flucytosine, then fluconazole/voriconazole after nonresponse, and died of worsening respiratory distress.
